latest_nl_proof:
Let
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
and
H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Assume (n-1)/n <= x < 1.

We first determine the floor terms.

For each k with 1 <= k < n, from x >= (n-1)/n we get
kx >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k < n, we have 0 < k/n < 1, hence k - k/n > k - 1. Also x < 1 implies kx < k. Therefore
k - 1 < kx < k,
so floor(kx) = k - 1.

For k = n, the hypothesis gives
n - 1 <= nx < n,
so floor(nx) = n - 1.

Substituting these values into F_n(x),
F_n(x) = (n - 1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k - 1)/k - (n - 1)/n.
Now
sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k - 1)/k = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (1 - 1/k) = (n - 1) - H_{n-1},
so
F_n(x) = (n - 1) - [(n - 1) - H_{n-1}] - (n - 1)/n
= H_{n-1} - (n - 1)/n.
Finally, since H_n = H_{n-1} + 1/n,
H_{n-1} - (n - 1)/n = H_{n-1} + 1/n - 1 = H_n - 1.
Hence F_n(x) = H_n - 1.
